inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start, injected into the system prompt and treated as the user's own instructions

instructions.note: Instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions, collapsing the trust boundary between persisted, unreviewed content and the authenticated user's direct commands.
mail.send can address any recipient with no approval gate, and drive.read covers the user's entire drive of confidential files, with no scoping to the task at hand.
'Anything useful' is undefined and unbounded, with no restriction against persisting content sourced from untrusted web pages fetched during research.

findings.title: Memory poisoning escalates recalled content to instruction authority, enabling persistent exfiltration (TC5 + TC3-like persistence + TC1)

attack_path.note: Untrusted web page fetched during research may contain content designed to look like a useful user preference or standing instruction.
Agent saves it via memory.save per prompt instruction to 'save anything useful'; no provenance is recorded and no human reviews the entry.
At the start of a later session the entry is recalled and injected into the system prompt, where the prompt explicitly instructs the agent to treat it as the user's own instruction.
The now-authoritative injected 'instruction' directs the agent to read confidential files from the user's full drive.
The agent sends the retrieved confidential content to an address with no approval gate or recipient allowlist.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: No present controls exist to decay further; watch for any widening of drive scope, any new egress-capable tool added to the agent, or a model upgrade, any of which would keep this path open or make it easier to trigger while memory remains unreviewed and unprovenanced.

evidence.observation: Prompt instructs the agent to save 'anything useful' to memory.save and to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions at the start of each session, with no filter on source trust.
memory.save accepts free text with no provenance, and the user never reviews saved entries; recalled memories are injected directly into the system prompt of every new session.
mail.send can send to any address without approval, and drive.read covers the user's full drive of confidential files.

recommendations.action: Enforce provenance/trust tagging at the memory store itself, and never grant recalled memory the same authority as a direct, authenticated user instruction; treat recalled memory as untrusted content requiring confirmation before it drives a sensitive action.
Require human approval with raw action review, plus a destination confirmation bound to a vetted contact record, before any mail.send.
Scope drive.read credentials to the specific folders needed for the current task instead of the entire drive.
Log all memory writes and outbound sends with content so incidents are attributable and reviewable.

findings.title: Direct lethal trifecta via indirect prompt injection in a single session (TC1), independent of memory

attack_path.note: Agent fetches an untrusted web page as part of research; the page contains injected instructions.
Injected instructions direct the agent to read confidential files from the user's drive.
Agent sends the retrieved confidential content externally with no approval gate or recipient allowlist.

forecast.watch_signal: No present controls exist to decay further; watch for any new egress-capable tool, widened drive scope, or model upgrade while mail.send and drive.read remain ungated.

evidence.observation: The agent's research function necessarily involves fetching and reading untrusted web content in the same context window as its privileged tool access.

drive.read covers the full drive of confidential files and mail.send can address any recipient with no approval gate, so a single session's untrusted web content can directly drive a read-then-send exfiltration without needing memory persistence.

recommendations.action: Require human approval with raw action review, plus a destination confirmation bound to a vetted contact record, before any mail.send, regardless of session.
Scope drive.read credentials to task-relevant folders, and spotlight/delimit fetched web content so it cannot be mistaken for an instruction within the same turn.

rating.rationale: Both findings start at critical (untrusted source reaching an irreversible, confidential-data egress sink) and no preventive, containment, or even detective control is declared anywhere in the design: memory.save has no provenance or review, drive.read is unscoped, and mail.send has no approval gate or recipient allowlist. With zero credited controls the residual floor equals the inherent tier for both findings, so the rollup stays at critical. The forecast also stays at critical for both findings, not because a future trigger would make things worse, but because nothing currently constrains the path for a trigger to defeat; the design is already at maximum exposure. The single highest-leverage fix is a structural pair: (1) provenance tagging enforced at the memory store so recalled content is never treated as equivalent to a direct user instruction (closes the memory-laundering finding at its root), and (2) a raw-action human approval gate with destination confirmation on mail.send bound to a vetted contact record (severs the final hop of both findings). Implementing either alone would drop its covered finding toward low per rubric section 5 step 1 or step 2; implementing neither leaves the agent at critical today with no further room to forecast.

limitations: This assessment reflects the design and configuration as declared in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of a deployed instance of this agent.

No formal tool manifest or MCP/API configuration was provided; capability fields such as credential_scope and maestro_layer are inferred from the prose description of memory.save, mail.send, and drive.read, so confidence on exact mechanism is medium even though the absence of controls is explicitly stated and rated high confidence.

No autonomy or runtime configuration (step limits, runtime limits, spawning behavior) was provided; autonomy.level is inferred as A3_act_then_report from context, and max_unattended_steps/max_runtime_minutes are treated as unbounded (null) because no limit is stated anywhere in the artifacts.
